```text
 Overview
  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.
  
  Functional Requirements
  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)
  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.
  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.
  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).
  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.
  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. Protection is active when
  game.numMoves < numMovesProtection (strictly less than); no winner can be declared during protection.
  Once game.numMoves >= numMovesProtection, protection ends and a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.
  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)
  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.
  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).
  Move Generation: Each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, source) method is responsible
  for returning the final list of legal moves for that piece. It must apply ALL
  applicable rules internally:
  - Global rules: source not vacant (VacantRule), source ≠ destination (NilMoveRule),
    within board boundaries (OutOfBoundaryRule), destination not friendly (OccupiedRule),
    and protection period check (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  - Piece-specific rules: Knight applies KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule;
    Archer applies ArcherMoveRule. A piece does NOT validate rules belonging to
    other piece types.
  Game.getAvailableMoves(player) simply iterates over all pieces belonging to the
  player, calls each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, position), and aggregates
  the results without additional filtering.
  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.
  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)
  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).
  Protection Rule: Protection is active when game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection.
  During protection, no piece can be captured (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.
  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).
  Board Display and Coordinates
  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x = column, y = row, both 0-based from
  bottom-left). Board reads should go through Game.getPiece(Place) or Game.getPiece(int x, int y). Board writes
  (e.g., in movePiece) should directly manipulate the 2D array via Game.getBoard()[x][y] = piece / null.
  There is no Game.setPiece() method. Direct indexing into board[][] is allowed for write operations in Game subclasses.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) prompts the user
  to choose a move from the list of available (already-validated legal) moves.

  Input format: The user enters a move as a coordinate "source->destination" (e.g., "a1->b2" means moving the piece at column a, row 1
  to column b, row 2).
  Coordinate parsing rules:
  - Column letter: 'a' maps to x=0, 'b' to x=1, 'c' to x=2, etc.
  - Row number: '1' maps to y=0, '2' to y=1, '3' to y=2, etc. (1-based to 0-based)
  - Parse source and destination separately using these rules.
  Validation: After parsing, the ConsolePlayer must verify that the parsed move
  (with matching source and destination coordinates) exists in availableMoves.
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools
  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:
  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
RandomPlayer::nextMove
Summary: Selects a random move from the list of available moves.
Algorithm:
  1. Generate a random index between 0 and availableMoves.size() - 1.
  2. Return the move at that index.
Related Features: None (uses List interface)
Related Classes: Move, Game
Input: game: Game - the current game state (not used);
       availableMoves: List<Move> - the list of pre-validated legal moves for this player.
Output: Move - a randomly selected move from the available list.
Pre-condition: availableMoves is non-empty.
Post-condition: Returns a valid move; game state is unchanged.

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

```java
public Move nextMove(final Game game, final EList<Move> availableMoves)
{
    java.util.Scanner scanner = new java.util.Scanner(System.in);
    while (true) {
        // a. Display the list of available moves
        System.out.println("Available moves:");
        for (int i = 0; i < availableMoves.size(); i++) {
            Move m = availableMoves.get(i);
            Place src = m.getSource();
            Place dst = m.getDestination();
            System.out.println((i + 1) + ": " + (char)('a' + src.getX()) + (src.getY() + 1) + "->" + (char)('a' + dst.getX()) + (dst.getY() + 1));
        }
        
        // b. Prompt the user
        System.out.print("Enter your move (source->destination, e.g., a1->b2): ");
        
        // c. Read input
        String input = scanner.nextLine().trim();
        
        // d. Parse input
        // i. Split by "->"
        String[] parts = input.split("->");
        if (parts.length != 2) {
            System.out.println("Error: Invalid format. Please use format 'source->destination'.");
            continue;
        }
        
        try {
            // ii. Parse source
            String srcStr = parts[0].trim();
            if (srcStr.length() < 2) {
                System.out.println("Error: Invalid source format.");
                continue;
            }
            int srcX = srcStr.charAt(0) - 'a';
            int srcY = Integer.parseInt(srcStr.substring(1)) - 1;
            
            // iii. Parse destination
            String dstStr = parts[1].trim();
            if (dstStr.length() < 2) {
                System.out.println("Error: Invalid destination format.");
                continue;
            }
            int dstX = dstStr.charAt(0) - 'a';
            int dstY = Integer.parseInt(dstStr.substring(1)) - 1;
            
            // iv. Check bounds
            if (srcX < 0 || dstX < 0 || srcY < 0 || dstY < 0) {
                System.out.println("Error: Invalid position (out of bounds).");
                continue;
            }
            
            // e. Create Move object
            Place source = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
            source.setX(srcX);
            source.setY(srcY);
            Place destination = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
            destination.setX(dstX);
            destination.setY(dstY);
            Move parsedMove = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createMove();
            parsedMove.setSource(source);
            parsedMove.setDestination(destination);
            
            // f. Check if this move exists in availableMoves
            for (Move availableMove : availableMoves) {
                if (availableMove.equal(parsedMove)) {
                    // g. Return the matching move
                    return availableMove;
                }
            }
            
            // h. If not found
            System.out.println("Error: The move is not valid. Please choose from the available moves.");
            
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            System.out.println("Error: Invalid number format.");
        } catch (StringIndexOutOfBoundsException e) {
            System.out.println("Error: Invalid input format.");
        }
    }
}
```

```java
        // i. Split by "->"
        String[] parts = input.split("->");
        if (parts.length != 2) {
            System.out.println("Error: Invalid format. Please use format 'source->destination'.");
            continue;
        }
        
        try {
            // ii. Parse source
            String srcStr = parts[0].trim();
            if (srcStr.length() < 2) {
                System.out.println("Error: Invalid source format.");
                continue;
            }
            int srcX = srcStr.charAt(0) - 'a';
            int srcY = Integer.parseInt(srcStr.substring(1)) - 1;

            if (dstStr.length() < 2) {
                System.out.println("Error: Invalid destination format.");

            System.out.println("Error: Invalid number format.");
        } catch (StringIndexOutOfBoundsException e) {

    }
```

        // f. Check if this move exists in availableMoves (using Move.equal() for comparison).
        for (Move availableMove : availableMoves) {
          // g. If found, return the matching move from availableMoves.
          if (availableMove.equal(parsedMove)) {
            return availableMove;
          }
        }
        
        // h. If not found, print error message and continue loop.
        System.out.println("Error: The move is not valid. Please choose from the available moves.");
        
      } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
        System.out.println("Error: Invalid number format.");
      } catch (StringIndexOutOfBoundsException e) {
        System.out.println("Error: Invalid input format.");
      }
    }
  }

} // ConsolePlayer

2. Define the 8 possible L-shaped offsets: (2,1), (2,-1), (-2,1), (-2,-1), (1,2), (1,-2), (-1,2), (-1,-2)
3. For each offset:

   b. Create a candidate Move(source, destination).
   c. Check all global rules: VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule.
   d. Check KnightMoveRule.
   e. Check KnightBlockRule.
   f. If all rules pass, add candidate move to the list.
4. Return the list of legal moves.

```java
  public EList<Move> getAvailableMoves(final Game game, final Place source)
  {
```
```java
    EList<Move> legalMoves = new BasicEList<Move>();
    
    // Define the 8 possible L-shaped offsets
    int[][] offsets = {
      {2, 1}, {2, -1}, {-2, 1}, {-2, -1},
      {1, 2}, {1, -2}, {-1, 2}, {-1, -2}
    };
    
    // Create rule instances
    VacantRule vacantRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createVacantRule();
    NilMoveRule nilMoveRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createNilMoveRule();
    OutOfBoundaryRule outOfBoundaryRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createOutOfBoundaryRule();
    OccupiedRule occupiedRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createOccupiedRule();
    FirstNMovesProtectionRule firstNMovesProtectionRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createFirstNMovesProtectionRule();
    KnightMoveRule knightMoveRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createKnightMoveRule();
    KnightBlockRule knightBlockRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createKnightBlockRule();
    
    for (int[] offset : offsets) {
      int dx = offset[0];
      int dy = offset[1];
      
      // Calculate destination
      Place destination = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
      destination.setX(source.getX() + dx);
      destination.setY(source.getY() + dy);
      
      // Create candidate move
      Move candidate = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createMove();
      candidate.setSource(source);
      candidate.setDestination(destination);
      
      // Check all global rules
      if (!vacantRule.validate(game, candidate)) continue;
      if (!nilMoveRule.validate(game, candidate)) continue;
      if (!outOfBoundaryRule.validate(game, candidate)) continue;
      if (!occupiedRule.validate(game, candidate)) continue;
      if (!firstNMovesProtectionRule.validate(game, candidate)) continue;
      
      // Check Knight-specific rules
      if (!knightMoveRule.validate(game, candidate)) continue;
      if (!knightBlockRule.validate(game, candidate)) continue;
      
      // All rules pass, add to list
      legalMoves.add(candidate);
    }
    
    return legalMoves;
  }
```

```java
   * Summary: Generates all legal moves for a Knight piece from a given source position.
   *          The Knight moves in an L-shape: 2 squares in one direction and 1 in the orthogonal direction.
   *          The move is blocked if there is a piece at the intermediate square (similar to Chinese chess Horse).
   *          Applies all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
   *          and Knight-specific rules (KnightMoveRule, KnightBlockRule).
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize an empty list of legal moves.
   *   2. Define the 8 possible L-shaped offsets:
   *      (2,1), (2,-1), (-2,1), (-2,-1), (1,2), (1,-2), (-1,2), (-1,-2)
   *   3. For each offset:
   *      a. Calculate destination = Place(source.x + dx, source.y + dy).
   *      b. Create a candidate Move(source, destination).
   *      c. Check all global rules: VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule.
   *      d. Check KnightMoveRule.
   *      e. Check KnightBlockRule.
   *      f. If all rules pass, add candidate move to the list.
   *   4. Return the list of legal moves.

   * Post-condition: Returns a list of valid moves; the game state is unchanged.
```

```java
  public EList<Move> getAvailableMoves(final Game game, final Place source)
  {
```
```java
    EList<Move> legalMoves = new BasicEList<Move>();
    
    // Define the 8 possible L-shaped offsets
    int[][] offsets = {
      {2, 1}, {2, -1}, {-2, 1}, {-2, -1},
      {1, 2}, {1, -2}, {-1, 2}, {-1, -2}
    };
    
    // Create rule instances
    VacantRule vacantRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createVacantRule();
    NilMoveRule nilMoveRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createNilMoveRule();
    OutOfBoundaryRule outOfBoundaryRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createOutOfBoundaryRule();
    OccupiedRule occupiedRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createOccupiedRule();
    FirstNMovesProtectionRule firstNMovesProtectionRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createFirstNMovesProtectionRule();
    KnightMoveRule knightMoveRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createKnightMoveRule();
    KnightBlockRule knightBlockRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createKnightBlockRule();
    
    for (int[] offset : offsets) {
      int dx = offset[0];
      int dy = offset[1];
      
      // Calculate destination
      Place destination = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
      destination.setX(source.getX() + dx);
      destination.setY(source.getY() + dy);
      
      // Create candidate move
      Move candidate = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createMove();
      candidate.setSource(source);
      candidate.setDestination(destination);
```

```java
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->

   * Summary: Generates all legal moves for a Knight piece from a given source position.
   *          The Knight moves in an L-shape: 2 squares in one direction and 1 in the orthogonal direction.
   *          The move is blocked if there is a piece at the intermediate square (similar to Chinese chess Horse).
   *          Applies all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
   *          and Knight-specific rules (KnightMoveRule, KnightBlockRule).
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize an empty list of legal moves.
   *   2. Define the 8 possible L-shaped offsets:
   *      (2,1), (2,-1), (-2,1), (-2,-1), (1,2), (1,-2), (-1,2), (-1,-2)
   *   3. For each offset:
   *      a. Calculate destination = Place(source.x + dx, source.y + dy).
   *      b. Create a candidate Move(source, destination).
   *      c. Check all global rules: VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule.
   *      d. Check KnightMoveRule.
   *      e. Check KnightBlockRule.
   *      f. If all rules pass, add candidate move to the list.
   *   4. Return the list of legal moves.
   * Related Features: Game.getPiece(Place), Game.getBoard(), Move.source, Move.destination, Place.x, Place.y, Game.configuration.size
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule, KnightMoveRule, KnightBlockRule
   * Input: game: Game - the current game state; source: Place - the position of the Knight piece.
   * Output: List<Move> - list of all legal moves for the Knight from the given source.
   * Pre-condition: The source position contains a Knight piece belonging to the current player.
   * Post-condition: Returns a list of valid moves; the game state is unchanged.

    };
```

```java
   *   2. Define the four orthogonal directions: (1,0), (-1,0), (0,1), (0,-1).
   *   3. For each direction:
   *      a. Set current position = source + direction.
   *      b. Initialize a piece counter = 0.
   *      c. While current position is within board boundaries:
   *         i.   If piece counter == 0:
   *              - If current square is empty, create candidate Move(source, current position).
   *                Check all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *         ii.  If piece counter == 1:
   *              - If current square has a piece (enemy), create candidate Move(source, current position).
   *                Check all global rules except OccupiedRule (since destination is occupied by enemy, not friendly)
   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *              - Break after processing this square (cannot move past a piece when capturing).
   *         iii. If current square has a piece (any color), increment piece counter.
   *         iv.  If piece counter >= 2, break (cannot jump over more than one piece).
   *         v.   Move to next square in the same direction (current += direction).
   *   4. Return the list of legal moves.
   * Related Features: Game.getPiece(Place), Game.getBoard(), Move.source, Move.destination, Place.x, Place.y
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule, ArcherMoveRule

   * Output: List<Move> - list of all legal moves for the Archer from the given source.
```

```java
   *          The Archer moves any distance orthogonally (up, down, left, right).
   *          For non-capturing moves, the path must be completely clear and destination must be empty.
   *          For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination (screen/mount),
   *          and the destination must contain an enemy piece.
   *          Applies all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)

   *   2. Define the four orthogonal directions: (1,0), (-1,0), (0,1), (0,-1).
   *   3. For each direction:

   *      b. Initialize a piece counter = 0.
   *      c. While current position is within board boundaries:
   *         i.   If piece counter == 0:
   *              - If current square is empty, create candidate Move(source, current position).
   *                Check all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)

   *                Check all global rules except OccupiedRule (since destination is occupied by enemy, not friendly)
   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *              - Break after processing this square (cannot move past a piece when capturing).
   *         iii. If current square has a piece (any color), increment piece counter.
   *         iv.  If piece counter >= 2, break (cannot jump over more than one piece).
```

```java
   * Summary: Generates all legal moves for an Archer piece from a given source position.
   *          The Archer moves any distance orthogonally (up, down, left, right).
   *          For non-capturing moves, the path must be completely clear and destination must be empty.
   *          For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination (screen/mount),
   *          and the destination must contain an enemy piece.
   *          Applies all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
   *          and the Archer-specific ArcherMoveRule.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize an empty list of legal moves.
   *   2. Define the four orthogonal directions: (1,0), (-1,0), (0,1), (0,-1).
   *   3. For each direction:
   *      a. Set current position = source + direction.
   *      b. Initialize a piece counter = 0.
   *      c. While current position is within board boundaries:
   *         i.   If piece counter == 0:
   *              - If current square is empty, create candidate Move(source, current position).
   *                Check all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *         ii.  If piece counter == 1:
   *              - If current square has a piece (enemy), create candidate Move(source, current position).
   *                Check all global rules except OccupiedRule (since destination is occupied by enemy, not friendly)
   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *              - Break after processing this square (cannot move past a piece when capturing).
   *         iii. If current square has a piece (any color), increment piece counter.
   *         iv.  If piece counter >= 2, break (cannot jump over more than one piece).
   *         v.   Move to next square in the same direction (current += direction).
   *   4. Return the list of legal moves.
   * Related Features: Game.getPiece(Place), Game.getBoard(), Move.source, Move.destination, Place.x, Place.y
```

```java
   *          For non-capturing moves, the path must be completely clear and destination must be empty.
   *          For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination (screen/mount),

   *      b. Initialize a piece counter = 0.
   *      c. While current position is within board boundaries:
   *         i.   If piece counter == 0:

   *                Check all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
```

```java
   *          For non-capturing moves, the path must be completely clear and destination must be empty.
   *          For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination (screen/mount),
```

  1.2 Locate these files in your project.
  1.3 Generate the class summarization.
2. A method is unimplemented if its body contains `// TODO: Please complete this Java method based on the docstring`.
3. For every unimplemented method, 
  3.1 You must read the docstring of this method. The fragment between `<!-- begin-model-doc -->` and `<!-- end-model-doc -->` contains the method specification;
  3.2 Generate your code strictly according to the algorithm; Be aware of the EMF code style and APIs;
  3.3 You should not change the method signature;
  3.4 After generation, replace the current body with the one you generate;
  3.5 Keep and update the docstring by changing `@generated` to `@generated NOT`.
4. Check the import list. Add missing imports if needed.
5. Do not change other part.
6. Be aware of the method signatures, particularly, the input and output types, provided in the context.

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

```java
   * Summary: Generates all legal moves for an Archer piece from a given source position.
   *          The Archer moves any distance orthogonally (up, down, left, right).
   *          For non-capturing moves, the path must be completely clear and destination must be empty.
   *          For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination (screen/mount),
   *          and the destination must contain an enemy piece.
   *          Applies all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
   *          and the Archer-specific ArcherMoveRule.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize an empty list of legal moves.
   *   2. Define the four orthogonal directions: (1,0), (-1,0), (0,1), (0,-1).
   *   3. For each direction:
   *      a. Set current position = source + direction.
   *      b. Initialize a piece counter = 0.
   *      c. While current position is within board boundaries:
   *         i.   If piece counter == 0:
   *              - If current square is empty, create candidate Move(source, current position).
   *                Check all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *         ii.  If piece counter == 1:
   *              - If current square has a piece (enemy), create candidate Move(source, current position).
   *                Check all global rules except OccupiedRule (since destination is occupied by enemy, not friendly)
   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *              - Break after processing this square (cannot move past a piece when capturing).
   *         iii. If current square has a piece (any color), increment piece counter.
   *         iv.  If piece counter >= 2, break (cannot jump over more than one piece).
   *         v.   Move to next square in the same direction (current += direction).
   *   4. Return the list of legal moves.
   * Related Features: Game.getPiece(Place), Game.getBoard(), Move.source, Move.destination, Place.x, Place.y
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule, ArcherMoveRule
   * Input: game: Game - the current game state; source: Place - the position of the Archer piece.
   * Output: List<Move> - list of all legal moves for the Archer from the given source.
   * Pre-condition: The source position contains an Archer piece belonging to the current player.
   * Post-condition: Returns a list of valid moves; the game state is unchanged.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated
   */
  public EList<Move> getAvailableMoves(final Game game, final Place source)
```

```java
   *          The Archer moves any distance orthogonally (up, down, left, right).
   *          For non-capturing moves, the path must be completely clear and destination must be empty.
   *          For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination (screen/mount),

   *                Check all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
```

public EList<Move> getAvailableMoves(final Game game, final Place source)
{
    EList<Move> legalMoves = new BasicEList<Move>();
    
    // Define four orthogonal directions
    int[][] directions = {{1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1}};
    
    // Get the board size
    int boardSize = game.getConfiguration().getSize();
    
    // Create instances of rules
    VacantRule vacantRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createVacantRule();
    NilMoveRule nilMoveRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createNilMoveRule();
    OutOfBoundaryRule outOfBoundaryRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createOutOfBoundaryRule();
    OccupiedRule occupiedRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createOccupiedRule();
    FirstNMovesProtectionRule firstNMovesProtectionRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createFirstNMovesProtectionRule();
    ArcherMoveRule archerMoveRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createArcherMoveRule();
    
    for (int[] dir : directions) {
        int dx = dir[0];
        int dy = dir[1];
        int cx = source.getX() + dx;
        int cy = source.getY() + dy;
        int pieceCounter = 0;
        
        while (cx >= 0 && cx < boardSize && cy >= 0 && cy < boardSize) {
            Piece pieceAtCurrent = game.getPiece(cx, cy);
            
            if (pieceCounter == 0) {
                if (pieceAtCurrent == null) {
                    // Create candidate move
                    Move candidate = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createMove();
                    candidate.setSource(source);
                    Place dest = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
                    dest.setX(cx);
                    dest.setY(cy);
                    candidate.setDestination(dest);
                    
                    // Check all global rules and ArcherMoveRule (except OccupiedRule since destination is empty)
                    if (vacantRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                        nilMoveRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                        outOfBoundaryRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                        firstNMovesProtectionRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                        archerMoveRule.validate(game, candidate)) {
                        legalMoves.add(candidate);
                    }
                }
            }
            
            if (pieceAtCurrent != null) {
                pieceCounter++;
            }
            
            if (pieceCounter == 1 && pieceAtCurrent != null) {
                // Check if it's an enemy piece
                Player currentPlayer = game.getCurrentPlayer();
                Player piecePlayer = pieceAtCurrent.getPlayer();
                if (piecePlayer != null && !piecePlayer.equals(currentPlayer)) {
                    // Create candidate move for capture
                    Move candidate = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createMove();
                    candidate.setSource(source);
                    Place dest = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
                    dest.setX(cx);
                    dest.setY(cy);
                    candidate.setDestination(dest);
                    
                    // Check all global rules except OccupiedRule (since destination is occupied by enemy)
                    // and ArcherMoveRule
                    if (nilMoveRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                        outOfBoundaryRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                        firstNMovesProtectionRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                        archerMoveRule.validate(game, candidate)) {
                        legalMoves.add(candidate);
                    }
                }
                break;
            }
            
            if (pieceCounter >= 2) {
                break;
            }
            
            cx += dx;
            cy += dy;
        }
    }
    
    return legalMoves;
}

```java
   *          For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination (screen/mount),

   *      c. While current position is within board boundaries:

   *                Check all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)

   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *              - Break after processing this square (cannot move past a piece when capturing).
   *         iii. If current square has a piece (any color), increment piece counter.
   *         iv.  If piece counter >= 2, break (cannot jump over more than one piece).
```

```java
   *          For non-capturing moves, the path must be completely clear and destination must be empty.
   *          For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination (screen/mount),
   *          and the destination must contain an enemy piece.

   *          and the Archer-specific ArcherMoveRule.

   *   2. Define the four orthogonal directions: (1,0), (-1,0), (0,1), (0,-1).
   *   3. For each direction:
   *      a. Set current position = source + direction.
   *      b. Initialize a piece counter = 0.
   *      c. While current position is within board boundaries:
   *         i.   If piece counter == 0:
   *              - If current square is empty, create candidate Move(source, current position).
   *                Check all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *         ii.  If piece counter == 1:
   *              - If current square has a piece (enemy), create candidate Move(source, current position).
   *                Check all global rules except OccupiedRule (since destination is occupied by enemy, not friendly)
   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *              - Break after processing this square (cannot move past a piece when capturing).
```

```java
   * Summary: Generates all legal moves for an Archer piece from a given source position.
   *          The Archer moves any distance orthogonally (up, down, left, right).
   *          For non-capturing moves, the path must be completely clear and destination must be empty.
   *          For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination (screen/mount),
   *          and the destination must contain an enemy piece.
   *          Applies all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
   *          and the Archer-specific ArcherMoveRule.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize an empty list of legal moves.
   *   2. Define the four orthogonal directions: (1,0), (-1,0), (0,1), (0,-1).
   *   3. For each direction:
   *      a. Set current position = source + direction.
   *      b. Initialize a piece counter = 0.
   *      c. While current position is within board boundaries:
   *         i.   If piece counter == 0:
   *              - If current square is empty, create candidate Move(source, current position).
   *                Check all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *         ii.  If piece counter == 1:
   *              - If current square has a piece (enemy), create candidate Move(source, current position).
   *                Check all global rules except OccupiedRule (since destination is occupied by enemy, not friendly)
   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *              - Break after processing this square (cannot move past a piece when capturing).
   *         iii. If current square has a piece (any color), increment piece counter.
   *         iv.  If piece counter >= 2, break (cannot jump over more than one piece).
   *         v.   Move to next square in the same direction (current += direction).
   *   4. Return the list of legal moves.
   * Related Features: Game.getPiece(Place), Game.getBoard(), Move.source, Move.destination, Place.x, Place.y
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule, ArcherMoveRule
   * Input: game: Game - the current game state; source: Place - the position of the Archer piece.
   * Output: List<Move> - list of all legal moves for the Archer from the given source.
   * Pre-condition: The source position contains an Archer piece belonging to the current player.
   * Post-condition: Returns a list of valid moves; the game state is unchanged.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
```

```java
   *          For non-capturing moves, the path must be completely clear and destination must be empty.
   *          For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination (screen/mount),

   *   3. For each direction:

   *      b. Initialize a piece counter = 0.
   *      c. While current position is within board boundaries:
   *         i.   If piece counter == 0:
   *              - If current square is empty, create candidate Move(source, current position).
   *                Check all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)

   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *              - Break after processing this square (cannot move past a piece when capturing).
```

```java
   *          For non-capturing moves, the path must be completely clear and destination must be empty.
   *          For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination (screen/mount),

   *                Check all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
```

```java
   *          The Archer moves any distance orthogonally (up, down, left, right).
   *          For non-capturing moves, the path must be completely clear and destination must be empty.
   *          For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination (screen/mount),
   *          and the destination must contain an enemy piece.
   *          Applies all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
   *          and the Archer-specific ArcherMoveRule.

   *   2. Define the four orthogonal directions: (1,0), (-1,0), (0,1), (0,-1).
   *   3. For each direction:

   *      b. Initialize a piece counter = 0.
   *      c. While current position is within board boundaries:
   *         i.   If piece counter == 0:
   *              - If current square is empty, create candidate Move(source, current position).
   *                Check all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)

   *                Check all global rules except OccupiedRule (since destination is occupied by enemy, not friendly)
   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *              - Break after processing this square (cannot move past a piece when capturing).
   *         iii. If current square has a piece (any color), increment piece counter.
   *         iv.  If piece counter >= 2, break (cannot jump over more than one piece).
   *         v.   Move to next square in the same direction (current += direction).
```

```java
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Generates all legal moves for an Archer piece from a given source position.
   *          The Archer moves any distance orthogonally (up, down, left, right).
   *          For non-capturing moves, the path must be completely clear and destination must be empty.
   *          For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination (screen/mount),
   *          and the destination must contain an enemy piece.
   *          Applies all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
   *          and the Archer-specific ArcherMoveRule.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize an empty list of legal moves.
   *   2. Define the four orthogonal directions: (1,0), (-1,0), (0,1), (0,-1).
   *   3. For each direction:
   *      a. Set current position = source + direction.
   *      b. Initialize a piece counter = 0.
   *      c. While current position is within board boundaries:
   *         i.   If piece counter == 0:
   *              - If current square is empty, create candidate Move(source, current position).
   *                Check all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *         ii.  If piece counter == 1:
   *              - If current square has a piece (enemy), create candidate Move(source, current position).
   *                Check all global rules except OccupiedRule (since destination is occupied by enemy, not friendly)
   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *              - Break after processing this square (cannot move past a piece when capturing).
   *         iii. If current square has a piece (any color), increment piece counter.
   *         iv.  If piece counter >= 2, break (cannot jump over more than one piece).
   *         v.   Move to next square in the same direction (current += direction).
   *   4. Return the list of legal moves.
   * Related Features: Game.getPiece(Place), Game.getBoard(), Move.source, Move.destination, Place.x, Place.y
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule, ArcherMoveRule
   * Input: game: Game - the current game state; source: Place - the position of the Archer piece.
   * Output: List<Move> - list of all legal moves for the Archer from the given source.
   * Pre-condition: The source position contains an Archer piece belonging to the current player.
   * Post-condition: Returns a list of valid moves; the game state is unchanged.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated
   */
```

```java
   *          For non-capturing moves, the path must be completely clear and destination must be empty.
   *          For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination (screen/mount),

   *      c. While current position is within board boundaries:

   *                Check all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)

   *              - Break after processing this square (cannot move past a piece when capturing).
   *         iii. If current square has a piece (any color), increment piece counter.
```

```java
   *          The Archer moves any distance orthogonally (up, down, left, right).
   *          For non-capturing moves, the path must be completely clear and destination must be empty.
   *          For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination (screen/mount),
   *          and the destination must contain an enemy piece.
   *          Applies all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)

   *   2. Define the four orthogonal directions: (1,0), (-1,0), (0,1), (0,-1).

   *      b. Initialize a piece counter = 0.
   *      c. While current position is within board boundaries:
   *         i.   If piece counter == 0:
   *              - If current square is empty, create candidate Move(source, current position).
   *                Check all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *         ii.  If piece counter == 1:
   *              - If current square has a piece (enemy), create candidate Move(source, current position).
   *                Check all global rules except OccupiedRule (since destination is occupied by enemy, not friendly)
   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *              - Break after processing this square (cannot move past a piece when capturing).
   *         iii. If current square has a piece (any color), increment piece counter.
   *         iv.  If piece counter >= 2, break (cannot jump over more than one piece).
   *         v.   Move to next square in the same direction (current += direction).
   *   4. Return the list of legal moves.
   * Related Features: Game.getPiece(Place), Game.getBoard(), Move.source, Move.destination, Place.x, Place.y
```

```java
   *          For non-capturing moves, the path must be completely clear and destination must be empty.
   *          For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination (screen/mount),

   *                Check all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
```

```java
   * Summary: Generates all legal moves for an Archer piece from a given source position.
   *          The Archer moves any distance orthogonally (up, down, left, right).
   *          For non-capturing moves, the path must be completely clear and destination must be empty.
   *          For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination (screen/mount),
   *          and the destination must contain an enemy piece.
   *          Applies all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
   *          and the Archer-specific ArcherMoveRule.
   * Algorithm:

   *   2. Define the four orthogonal directions: (1,0), (-1,0), (0,1), (0,-1).
   *   3. For each direction:
   *      a. Set current position = source + direction.
   *      b. Initialize a piece counter = 0.
   *      c. While current position is within board boundaries:
   *         i.   If piece counter == 0:
   *              - If current square is empty, create candidate Move(source, current position).
   *                Check all global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule)
   *                and ArcherMoveRule. If all pass, add to list.
   *         ii.  If piece counter == 1:

public EList<Move> getAvailableMoves(final Game game, final Place source)
{
```

```java
    int[][] directions = {{1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1}};

    VacantRule vacantRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createVacantRule();
    NilMoveRule nilMoveRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createNilMoveRule();
    OutOfBoundaryRule outOfBoundaryRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createOutOfBoundaryRule();
    OccupiedRule occupiedRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createOccupiedRule();
    FirstNMovesProtectionRule firstNMovesProtectionRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createFirstNMovesProtectionRule();
    ArcherMoveRule archerMoveRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createArcherMoveRule();
    
    for (int[] dir : directions) {

        int dy = dir[1];
        
        int curX = source.getX() + dx;
        int curY = source.getY() + dy;
        int pieceCounter = 0;
        
        while (curX >= 0 && curX < boardSize && curY >= 0 && curY < boardSize) {
            Place dest = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();

                if (pieceAtDest == null) {

                        occupiedRule.validate(game, candidate) &&

                pieceCounter++;
            }

                if (vacantRule.validate(game, candidate) &&

                    outOfBoundaryRule.validate(game, candidate) &&

                    legalMoves.add(candidate);
                }
                break;
```

```java
  public EList<Move> getAvailableMoves(final Game game, final Place source)
  {
    EList<Move> legalMoves = new BasicEList<Move>();
    
    int[][] directions = {{1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1}};
    int boardSize = game.getConfiguration().getSize();
    
    VacantRule vacantRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createVacantRule();
    NilMoveRule nilMoveRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createNilMoveRule();
    OutOfBoundaryRule outOfBoundaryRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createOutOfBoundaryRule();
    OccupiedRule occupiedRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createOccupiedRule();
    FirstNMovesProtectionRule firstNMovesProtectionRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createFirstNMovesProtectionRule();
    ArcherMoveRule archerMoveRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createArcherMoveRule();
    
    for (int[] dir : directions) {
      int dx = dir[0];
      int dy = dir[1];
      
      int curX = source.getX() + dx;
      int curY = source.getY() + dy;
      int pieceCounter = 0;
      
      while (curX >= 0 && curX < boardSize && curY >= 0 && curY < boardSize) {
        Place dest = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
        dest.setX(curX);
        dest.setY(curY);
        
        Piece pieceAtDest = game.getPiece(dest);
        
        if (pieceCounter == 0) {
          if (pieceAtDest == null) {
            Move candidate = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createMove();
            candidate.setSource(source);
            candidate.setDestination(dest);
            
            if (vacantRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                nilMoveRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                outOfBoundaryRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                occupiedRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                firstNMovesProtectionRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                archerMoveRule.validate(game, candidate)) {
              legalMoves.add(candidate);
            }
          }
        }
```
        
```java
        if (pieceCounter == 1) {
          if (pieceAtDest != null) {
            Move candidate = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createMove();
            candidate.setSource(source);
            candidate.setDestination(dest);
            
            if (vacantRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                nilMoveRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                outOfBoundaryRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                firstNMovesProtectionRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                archerMoveRule.validate(game, candidate)) {
              legalMoves.add(candidate);
            }
            break;
          }
        }
        
        if (pieceAtDest != null) {
          pieceCounter++;
        }
        
        if (pieceCounter >= 2) {
          break;
        }
        
        curX += dx;
        curY += dy;
      }
```
```java
    }
    
    return legalMoves;
  }
}
```

```java
   *          For non-capturing moves, the path must be completely clear and destination must be empty.
   *          For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination (screen/mount),
```

```java
    OutOfBoundaryRule outOfBoundaryRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createOutOfBoundaryRule();

    ArcherMoveRule archerMoveRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createArcherMoveRule();

      int dx = dir[0];
      int dy = dir[1];
      
      int curX = source.getX() + dx;
      int curY = source.getY() + dy;
      int pieceCounter = 0;
      
      while (curX >= 0 && curX < boardSize && curY >= 0 && curY < boardSize) {
        Place dest = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
        dest.setX(curX);
        dest.setY(curY);
```

```java
        if (pieceCounter == 1) {

            Move candidate = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createMove();
            candidate.setSource(source);
            candidate.setDestination(dest);
            
            if (vacantRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                nilMoveRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                outOfBoundaryRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                firstNMovesProtectionRule.validate(game, candidate) &&
                archerMoveRule.validate(game, candidate)) {
              legalMoves.add(candidate);
            }
            break;
          }
        }
        
        if (pieceAtDest != null) {
          pieceCounter++;
        }
        
        if (pieceCounter >= 2) {

        }

        curY += dy;
```

/**
 * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
 * <!-- end-user-doc -->
 * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
 * Summary: Validates that the destination square does not contain a piece of the same player (friendly piece). Capturing an opponent's piece is allowed.
 * Algorithm:
 *   1. Get the piece at the destination using game.getPiece(move.destination).
 *   2. If destination is empty (null), return true.
 *   3. Get the piece at the source using game.getPiece(move.source).
 *   4. If both pieces belong to the same player (sourcePiece.player == destinationPiece.player), return false.
 *   5. Otherwise return true (destination has opponent piece or is empty).
 * Related Features: Game.getPiece(Place), Move.source, Move.destination, Piece.player
 * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece, Player
 * Input: game: Game - the current game state; move: Move - the move to validate.
 * Output: boolean - true if destination is empty or contains an opponent piece, false if contains friendly piece.
 * Pre-condition: Source is not vacant (has a piece).
 * Post-condition: Returns validation result; game state is unchanged.
 * <!-- end-model-doc -->
 * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
 * @generated NOT
 */
public boolean validate(final Game game, final Move move)
{
    // Get the piece at the destination
    Piece destinationPiece = game.getPiece(move.getDestination());
    
    // If destination is empty (null), return true
    if (destinationPiece == null) {
        return true;
    }
    
    // Get the piece at the source
    Piece sourcePiece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
    
    // If both pieces belong to the same player, return false
    if (sourcePiece.getPlayer() == destinationPiece.getPlayer()) {
        return false;
    }
    
    // Otherwise return true (destination has opponent piece)
    return true;
}

   * Pre-condition: Source is not vacant (has a piece).
   * Post-condition: Returns validation result; game state is unchanged.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean validate(final Game game, final Move move)
  {
    Piece destinationPiece = game.getPiece(move.getDestination());
    if (destinationPiece == null) {
      return true;
    }
    Piece sourcePiece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
    if (sourcePiece.getPlayer() == destinationPiece.getPlayer()) {
      return false;
    }
    return true;
  }

    int sy = source.getY();
    int dx = destination.getX();
    int dy = destination.getY();
    
    int diffX = Math.abs(dx - sx);

```java
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Validates that the Knight's move is not blocked by a piece at the intermediate square.
   *          If moving 2 squares horizontally and 1 vertically, blocking square is at ((sx+dx)/2, sy).
   *          If moving 1 square horizontally and 2 vertically, blocking square is at (sx, (sy+dy)/2).
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Extract source (sx, sy) and destination (dx, dy) from the move.
   *   2. Calculate the absolute differences: diffX = |dx - sx|, diffY = |dy - sy|.
   *   3. If (diffX == 2 and diffY == 1):
   *      a. blockingX = (sx + dx) / 2
   *      b. blockingY = sy
   *   4. Else if (diffX == 1 and diffY == 2):
   *      a. blockingX = sx
   *      b. blockingY = (sy + dy) / 2
   *   5. Else: return true (not a valid Knight move, but this rule only checks blocking).
   *   6. Get the piece at the blocking square using game.getPiece(blockingX, blockingY).
   *   7. If the blocking square is not empty, return false (blocked).
   *   8. Return true (no block).
   * Related Features: Game.getPiece(int x, int y), Move.source, Move.destination, Place.x, Place.y
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place
   * Input: game: Game - the current game state; move: Move - the move to validate.
   * Output: boolean - true if the move is not blocked, false if blocked.
   * Pre-condition: The source contains a Knight piece; the move has passed KnightMoveRule.
```

```java
   * Summary: Validates that the Knight's move is not blocked by a piece at the intermediate square.
   *          If moving 2 squares horizontally and 1 vertically, blocking square is at ((sx+dx)/2, sy).
   *          If moving 1 square horizontally and 2 vertically, blocking square is at (sx, (sy+dy)/2).
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Extract source (sx, sy) and destination (dx, dy) from the move.
   *   2. Calculate the absolute differences: diffX = |dx - sx|, diffY = |dy - sy|.
   *   3. If (diffX == 2 and diffY == 1):
   *      a. blockingX = (sx + dx) / 2
   *      b. blockingY = sy
   *   4. Else if (diffX == 1 and diffY == 2):
   *      a. blockingX = sx
   *      b. blockingY = (sy + dy) / 2
   *   5. Else: return true (not a valid Knight move, but this rule only checks blocking).
   *   6. Get the piece at the blocking square using game.getPiece(blockingX, blockingY).
   *   7. If the blocking square is not empty, return false (blocked).
   *   8. Return true (no block).
   * Related Features: Game.getPiece(int x, int y), Move.source, Move.destination, Place.x, Place.y
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place
   * Input: game: Game - the current game state; move: Move - the move to validate.
   * Output: boolean - true if the move is not blocked, false if blocked.
   * Pre-condition: The source contains a Knight piece; the move has passed KnightMoveRule.
   * Post-condition: Returns validation result; game state is unchanged.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
```
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean validate(final Game game, final Move move)
  {
    // Extract source (sx, sy) and destination (dx, dy) from the move
    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place destination = move.getDestination();
    int sx = source.getX();
    int sy = source.getY();
    int dx = destination.getX();
    int dy = destination.getY();

    // Calculate the absolute differences
    int diffX = Math.abs(dx - sx);
    int diffY = Math.abs(dy - sy);

    int blockingX;
    int blockingY;

    if (diffX == 2 && diffY == 1) {
      // Moving 2 squares horizontally and 1 vertically
      blockingX = (sx + dx) / 2;
      blockingY = sy;
    } else if (diffX == 1 && diffY == 2) {
      // Moving 1 square horizontally and 2 vertically
      blockingX = sx;
      blockingY = (sy + dy) / 2;
    } else {
      // Not a valid Knight move, but this rule only checks blocking
      return true;
    }

    // Get the piece at the blocking square
    Piece piece = game.getPiece(blockingX, blockingY);

    // If the blocking square is not empty, return false (blocked)
    if (piece != null) {
      return false;
    }

    return true;

```java
public boolean validate(final Game game, final Move move)
{
    // Extract source and destination
    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place destination = move.getDestination();
    int sx = source.getX();
    int sy = source.getY();
    int dx = destination.getX();
    int dy = destination.getY();
    
    // Check if move is orthogonal: (sx == dx) XOR (sy == dy)
    if ((sx == dx) == (sy == dy)) {
        return false;
    }
    
    // Determine direction and number of steps
    int stepX = (dx == sx) ? 0 : (dx > sx ? 1 : -1);
    int stepY = (dy == sy) ? 0 : (dy > sy ? 1 : -1);
    int steps = Math.max(Math.abs(dx - sx), Math.abs(dy - sy));
    
    // Count pieces between source and destination (exclusive)
    int pieceCount = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i < steps; i++) {
        int cx = sx + i * stepX;
        int cy = sy + i * stepY;
        if (game.getPiece(cx, cy) != null) {
            pieceCount++;
        }
    }
    
    // Get piece at destination
    Piece destPiece = game.getPiece(destination);
    
    // If destination is empty
    if (destPiece == null) {
        return pieceCount == 0;
    }
    // If destination is occupied (capture)
    else {
        return pieceCount == 1;
    }
```

```java
public boolean validate(final Game game, final Move move)
{
    // Extract source and destination
    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place destination = move.getDestination();
    int sx = source.getX();
    int sy = source.getY();
    int dx = destination.getX();
    int dy = destination.getY();
    
    // Check if move is orthogonal: (sx == dx) XOR (sy == dy)
    if ((sx == dx) == (sy == dy)) {
        return false;
    }
    
    // Determine direction and number of steps
    int stepX = (dx == sx) ? 0 : (dx > sx ? 1 : -1);
    int stepY = (dy == sy) ? 0 : (dy > sy ? 1 : -1);
    int steps = Math.max(Math.abs(dx - sx), Math.abs(dy - sy));
    
    // Count pieces between source and destination (exclusive)
    int pieceCount = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i < steps; i++) {
        int cx = sx + i * stepX;
        int cy = sy + i * stepY;
        if (game.getPiece(cx, cy) != null) {
            pieceCount++;
        }
    }
    
    // Get piece at destination
    Piece destPiece = game.getPiece(destination);
    
    // If destination is empty
    if (destPiece == null) {
        return pieceCount == 0;
    }
    // If destination is occupied (capture)
    else {
        return pieceCount == 1;
    }
}
```

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Validates that a move conforms to the Archer movement rules:
   *          - The move must be strictly orthogonal (same x or same y).
   *          - For non-capturing moves (destination empty): all squares between source and destination must be empty.
   *          - For capturing moves (destination occupied): there must be exactly one piece (any color) between source and destination.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Extract source (sx, sy) and destination (dx, dy) from the move.
   *   2. Check if move is orthogonal: (sx == dx) XOR (sy == dy). If not, return false.
   *   3. Determine the direction and number of steps.
   *   4. Count pieces between source and destination (exclusive of source and destination).
   *   5. Get the piece at destination using game.getPiece(destination).
   *   6. If destination is empty (null): return true if piece count == 0, else false.
   *   7. If destination is occupied (capture): return true if piece count == 1, else false.
   * Related Features: Game.getPiece(Place), Move.source, Move.destination, Place.x, Place.y
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place
   * Input: game: Game - the current game state; move: Move - the move to validate.
   * Output: boolean - true if the move is valid according to Archer movement rules, false otherwise.
   * Pre-condition: The source contains an Archer piece; source and destination are within board boundaries.
   * Post-condition: Returns validation result; game state is unchanged.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean validate(final Game game, final Move move)
  {
    // Extract source (sx, sy) and destination (dx, dy) from the move
    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place destination = move.getDestination();
    int sx = source.getX();
    int sy = source.getY();
    int dx = destination.getX();
    int dy = destination.getY();

    // Check if move is orthogonal: (sx == dx) XOR (sy == dy)
    if ((sx == dx) == (sy == dy)) {
      return false;
    }

    // Determine the direction and number of steps
    int stepX = (dx == sx) ? 0 : (dx > sx ? 1 : -1);
    int stepY = (dy == sy) ? 0 : (dy > sy ? 1 : -1);
    int steps = Math.max(Math.abs(dx - sx), Math.abs(dy - sy));

    // Count pieces between source and destination (exclusive of source and destination)
    int pieceCount = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i < steps; i++) {
      int cx = sx + i * stepX;
      int cy = sy + i * stepY;
      if (game.getPiece(cx, cy) != null) {
        pieceCount++;
      }
    }

    // Get the piece at destination using game.getPiece(destination)
    Piece destPiece = game.getPiece(destination);

    // If destination is empty (null): return true if pieceCount == 0, else false
    if (destPiece == null) {
      return pieceCount == 0;
    }
    // If destination is occupied (capture): return true if pieceCount == 1, else false
    else {
      return pieceCount == 1;
    }
  }

# Task
You will be given a **Requirement** and a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML. Your task is to annotate every operation listed in **Operations** with a specification.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pseudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Take the principle of modularization into account.
2. For each operation, determine its functional boundary based on the given requirement. Ensure high cohesion and low coupling.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview
  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.
  
  Functional Requirements
  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)
  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.
  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.
  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).
  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.
  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. Protection is active when
  game.numMoves < numMovesProtection (strictly less than); no winner can be declared during protection.
  Once game.numMoves >= numMovesProtection, protection ends and a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.
  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)
  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.
  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).
  Move Generation: Each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, source) method is responsible
  for returning the final list of legal moves for that piece. It must apply ALL
  applicable rules internally:
  - Global rules: source not vacant (VacantRule), source ≠ destination (NilMoveRule),
    within board boundaries (OutOfBoundaryRule), destination not friendly (OccupiedRule),
    and protection period check (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  - Piece-specific rules: Knight applies KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule;
    Archer applies ArcherMoveRule. A piece does NOT validate rules belonging to
    other piece types.
  Game.getAvailableMoves(player) simply iterates over all pieces belonging to the
  player, calls each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, position), and aggregates
  the results without additional filtering.
  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.
  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)
  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).
  Protection Rule: Protection is active when game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection.
  During protection, no piece can be captured (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.
  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).
  Board Display and Coordinates
  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x = column, y = row, both 0-based from
  bottom-left). Board reads should go through Game.getPiece(Place) or Game.getPiece(int x, int y). Board writes
  (e.g., in movePiece) should directly manipulate the 2D array via Game.getBoard()[x][y] = piece / null.
  There is no Game.setPiece() method. Direct indexing into board[][] is allowed for write operations in Game subclasses.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) prompts the user
  to choose a move from the list of available (already-validated legal) moves.

  Input format: The user enters a move as a coordinate "source->destination" (e.g., "a1->b2" means moving the piece at column a, row 1
  to column b, row 2).
  Coordinate parsing rules:
  - Column letter: 'a' maps to x=0, 'b' to x=1, 'c' to x=2, etc.
  - Row number: '1' maps to y=0, '2' to y=1, '3' to y=2, etc. (1-based to 0-based)
  - Parse source and destination separately using these rules.
  Validation: After parsing, the ConsolePlayer must verify that the parsed move
  (with matching source and destination coordinates) exists in availableMoves.
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools
  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:
  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```

{org.eclipse.emf.ecore.impl.EOperationImpl@44af21cf (name: getWinner) (ordered: true, unique: true, lowerBound: 0, upperBound: 1)=Summary: Determines the winner of the game after a move has been executed, considering protection phase and win conditions.
Algorithm:
  1. If game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection (protection active), return null (no winner).
  2. Check win condition 1: If lastPiece is a Knight AND lastMove.source equals centralPlace AND lastMove.destination does NOT equal centralPlace, return the opponent of lastPlayer.
  3. Check win condition 2: Count remaining pieces of each player on the board.
     a. If only one player has pieces remaining, return that player.
  4. Check win condition 3: If the current player (next player after lastPlayer) has no available moves:
     a. Compare scores of both players.
     b. If lastPlayer's score > opponent's score, return lastPlayer.
     c. If opponent's score > lastPlayer's score, return opponent.
     d. If scores are equal, return the current player (who has no moves).
  5. If no win condition is met, return null.
Related Features: game.numMoves, configuration.numMovesProtection, game.getCentralPlace(), game.getPiece(Place), game.getAvailableMoves(Player), Move.source, Move.destination, Player.score
Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece, Knight, Player, Configuration
Input: lastPlayer - the player who just made the move; lastPiece - the piece that was moved; lastMove - the move that was executed
